source.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
source.date_note: First submitted to arXiv on 2022-10-06; arXiv v3 was revised on 2023-03-10 and identified as the ICLR 2023 camera-ready version.

insight.title: ReAct: reason, act, observe — then update the plan
insight.one_liner: ReAct interleaves model reasoning with external actions and observations so each can update the next step; it improves grounding but is not a production control layer.
insight.why_this_matters: ReAct is a useful mental model for the inside of an agent loop. It explains how a model can alternate between thinking and interacting with an environment, while making clear why a separate execution layer is still required for authorization, reliable side effects, recovery and audit.

whole_source_map.problem: Reason-only trajectories can remain ungrounded and propagate hallucinated facts, while action-only trajectories can interact with an environment without enough high-level reasoning to plan, interpret observations or recover from mistakes.
whole_source_map.thesis: Interleave language reasoning traces with task-specific actions and environment observations so reasoning guides acting while external feedback grounds and updates subsequent reasoning.
core_topics: language reasoning as an augmented action space
loop, retrieval and context-length failure modes
action selection versus production execution control

derived_model.problem: A model that only reasons can drift away from external facts, while a model that only acts can lack an explicit mechanism for planning and interpreting feedback.
derived_model.mechanism: Let the model emit a reasoning step, choose an environment action, receive an observation, and fold that observation back into the next reasoning/action decision; reasoning can be dense or sparse depending on the task.
derived_model.result: The trajectory can become more grounded and diagnosable, but the loop still needs an external production layer to authorize and safely execute consequential actions.

central_chain: Reason-only methods have no built-in external feedback loop, while act-only methods can lack enough high-level planning context.
ReAct adds language thoughts to the agent trajectory and interleaves them with environment actions and observations.
Reasoning helps choose and reformulate actions; observations inject external evidence that can change subsequent reasoning.
The feedback loop improves grounding in the paper's tasks but can still repeat bad reasoning or be derailed by poor retrieval.
Therefore ReAct is best understood as an action-selection/cognitive loop, not as the authorization, durability or audit substrate around real production actions.
open_gaps: The experiments use 2022-era PaLM/GPT-3 models, so benchmark numbers are historical evidence for the method rather than current model rankings.
Modern native tool-calling systems may implement the same feedback principle without exposing free-form reasoning traces; that is a useful follow-up source rather than a claim made by this paper.

nodes.label: 01 · Reason
nodes.title: Thought
nodes.text: Compose useful context: decompose the goal, track progress, interpret evidence or reformulate the plan.

nodes.label: 02 · Act
nodes.title: Environment action
nodes.text: Search, look up, navigate or perform another task-specific action that can change or query the environment.

nodes.label: 03 · Observe
nodes.title: External feedback
nodes.text: The environment returns evidence or state that becomes new context rather than leaving reasoning closed over internal knowledge.

nodes.label: 04 · Update
nodes.title: Next decision
nodes.text: The model uses the expanded trajectory to continue, reformulate, finish or choose another action.

image.reason: The teaching value is in a feedback sequence and the boundary between action selection and execution control; a diagram is more precise than a generated illustration.

concepts.name: ReAct loop
concepts.why_needed: The core unit is not a single prompt but a trajectory where reasoning, action and observation repeatedly update one another.

concepts.name: Reasoning trace
concepts.why_needed: In the paper a thought is a language-space step that updates the model's context without itself changing the external environment.

concepts.name: Observation grounding
concepts.why_needed: Actions are valuable partly because the returned observation can inject external evidence and alter the next decision.

concepts.name: Action selection versus execution
concepts.why_needed: ReAct can propose the next action; production systems still need separate authority, enforcement, recovery and verification around consequential execution.

examples.scenario: A question requires facts that are uncertain or absent from the model's internal context.
examples.question: Can the model explicitly decide what to retrieve, use the returned observation, and revise the next step instead of completing a closed reasoning chain?

examples.scenario: An agent searches an environment for an object and then must switch from exploration to completing the goal.
examples.question: Can sparse reasoning track progress and update the plan after observations rather than blindly emitting the next action?

examples.scenario: A ReAct-style loop proposes a consequential tool call such as changing business data.
examples.question: What separate layer checks authority, executes idempotently, records evidence and verifies the outcome after the model selects the action?

limitations: ReAct can enter repetitive thought/action loops; an observation does not guarantee the model will reason its way out of a bad trajectory.
Non-informative retrieval can derail subsequent reasoning, making tool quality and observation design part of agent quality.
Complex tasks with large action spaces need more demonstrations and can hit in-context length limits under the paper's prompting setup.
The paper's benchmark action spaces are constrained and intentionally safe; connecting an LLM to real external actions introduces risks the paper does not solve.
Visible reasoning traces improve diagnosability in this setup but should not be treated as a durable, complete or trustworthy audit record of production execution.

use_now: Separate two design questions when reviewing an agent: how does the model choose the next action, and how does the system control execution of that action?
Treat observations as first-class inputs to the next decision rather than simply tool outputs to display.
try: Build a tiny read-only ReAct loop with one search/lookup tool, a strict maximum step count and an explicit repeated-state breaker.
Log Thought/Action/Observation as diagnostic development data, then compare it with the separate execution evidence you would need for a consequential tool call.
learn: the boundary between model trajectory and controlled execution
build: A minimal agent-loop demo where read-only retrieval is allowed directly but a simulated write action is handed to a separate policy/execution boundary.
watch: How modern native tool-calling agents preserve the ReAct feedback principle while hiding or restructuring free-form reasoning traces.
ignore_for_now: The paper's absolute 2022-era PaLM benchmark scores as a ranking of current agent systems.

connections: controlled execution: ReAct selects or proposes actions; the existing controlled-execution concept governs consequential execution after selection
execution history: a reasoning trace can explain a model trajectory but is not the same as durable evidence of authority, versions, external side effects and verification
retrieval quality: bad observations can become a direct failure input to later reasoning
agent evaluation: trajectory failures can be classified as reasoning loops, retrieval failures, hallucination or task/label mismatch

concepts.label: ReAct loop
concepts.summary: An agent trajectory that interleaves language reasoning, environment actions and returned observations so each step can update the next decision.

concepts.label: Reasoning trace
concepts.summary: A language-space step used to compose task context, plans or interpretations without itself changing the external environment.

concepts.label: Observation grounding
concepts.summary: Using evidence returned by an external action or environment to update the context for subsequent reasoning and action selection.

relations.rationale: ReAct adds explicit language reasoning steps that maintain plans, interpret observations and support later action choices.
The loop is grounded by observations returned from environment actions; without useful feedback it can continue or reformulate poorly.
ReAct explains how a model selects and updates actions, while controlled execution governs whether consequential actions are authorized, safely executed, reconstructed and verified.
